workloads.label: Storage & egress · 100 GiB storage, 50 GiB egress
caveats: Metered compute is NOT priced here. This figure covers only a plan's fixed fee, storage, and egress — it is not the cost of running a database.

That omission cuts one way: a provider that folds compute into a fixed plan fee (Supabase, PlanetScale) has that compute counted, while a provider that meters compute separately (Neon, billed per CU-hour) has none of it counted and looks cheaper than it would on a like-for-like basis.

Egress is optional: where a provider has no recorded egress_gib row, this figure excludes egress entirely. It does not mean egress is free — it means either the provider bundles it at no separate charge (recorded as a $0 rate with a source) or no per-GB rate has been published. Do not read a figure with no egress row as proof egress is included.
Excludes support plans, committed-use discounts, and negotiated enterprise pricing.
Excludes backups beyond default retention and cross-region transfer.

caveats: Metered compute is NOT priced here. This figure covers only a plan's fixed fee, storage, and egress — it is not the cost of running a database.

Egress is optional: where a provider has no recorded egress_gib row, this figure excludes egress entirely. workloads.label: Cheapest plan with 100 GiB storage
caveats: This compares plan fees only — it excludes metered compute and egress.
It can only consider plans whose included storage has been recorded; a provider offering a qualifying plan that has not been observed yet will show as insufficient data, not as expensive.

workloads.label: Block storage · 500 GiB SSD volume
caveats: Only SSD-class general-purpose volume types are compared; HDD and archival tiers (AWS st1/sc1, Azure Standard HDD, GCP Standard PD) are excluded — a cheap cold-HDD rate winning against an SSD-only provider would be a false comparison, not a cheap one.

This figure assumes the performance baseline included with the volume and excludes provisioned IOPS or throughput bought beyond it. Where the vendor states a free baseline (AWS gp3: 3,000 IOPS/125 MB/s; Azure Premium SSD v2: 3,000 IOPS/125 MB/s; GCP Hyperdisk Balanced: 3,000 IOPS/140 MBps), that baseline is what's priced here — a workload needing more pays additional metered charges not reflected in this total.

Fixed-tier bucketed disk products (e.g. Azure Premium SSD P-series, Standard SSD E-series) are not recorded under this metric: they are sold as discrete disk-size SKUs rather than a continuous per-GiB rate, and a derived rate would misrepresent how they're actually billed.
Prices are region-dependent; figures are for us-east or the closest selectable equivalent — see each row's note for the exact region read.
Excludes snapshots, data transfer, compute, and any charge other than provisioned volume capacity — this prices an attached block volume only, not a virtual machine or the compute needed to use it.

workloads.label: Snapshot storage · 100 GiB retained
caveats: Prices 100 GiB of retained snapshot data, not a backup schedule: AWS, Azure, and GCP bill snapshots incrementally on changed blocks, so what a given backup schedule actually retains depends on a churn rate no vendor publishes. This is not 'the cost of daily snapshots.'

Compares standard snapshot tiers only. Archive and cold tiers are cheaper per GiB-month but carry retrieval charges and minimum retention periods, so a monthly rate alone understates them and would not be comparable with a standard tier.

Where a provider publishes multiple snapshot storage tiers (e.g. AWS/GCP Standard vs. Archive), the cheapest recorded tier is shown; a cheaper archive-class tier can carry retrieval fees and a minimum retention period not reflected in this monthly figure — see the provider's rows for details.
DigitalOcean's page states a flat per-GiB snapshot rate but does not say whether it is a full copy or an incremental delta; it is recorded as published, without assuming either.
Prices are region-dependent; figures are for us-east or the closest selectable equivalent — see each row's note for the exact region read.
Excludes compute and the source volume's own capacity charge — this prices retained snapshot storage only.
